clue.text: Figure at one stage included in dance, finally cut

indicators.note: the phrase at one stage is placed inside the trimmed dance
the dance loses its final letter, as the clue tells us to cut its end

parts.note: the quadrille is a square dance for four couples
taken as written
an era is one stage or period of history

explanation.surface: A dance figure once performed inside a routine whose ending was dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' is the definition in its geometric sense, not a dance figure; 'finally cut' removes only the last letter of the dance, and 'included in' sets the phrase before its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided shape is a geometrical figure of that name.

clue.text: One's quite smart — could become chairman

indicators.note: could become suggests these words turning into something else, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever person might rise to lead the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The host of a quiz presides over it, acting as its chairman.

clue.text: Quickly producing pop-up card

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for pop is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, as is pa
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A pop-up greeting card produced in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at speed means doing something swiftly.

clue.text: Create it as rude as possible

indicators.note: possible hints at a potential other arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to be as offensive as one can.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a fuss or commotion, so to create in the sense of causing trouble.

clue.text: Erudite humorist, Edward

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse and limericks
Ned is a pet form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A scholarly comic writer named Edward, as Lear was.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-read, scholarly person is described as erudite.

clue.text: Principle English men introduced to other people

indicators.note: introduced to means the English men are put inside the word for other people

parts.note: them refers to other people, not us
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A principle of English gentlemen being presented to foreigners.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition established by reasoning is a mathematical principle.

clue.text: Stratagem it's right to employ

parts.note: to use is to employ

explanation.surface: Justifying a trick as fair to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A trick or deception is a stratagem.

clue.text: Let eyes follow mind

parts.note: to let your eyes rest on something is to look
to come after is to follow

explanation.surface: Advice to watch one's step and follow carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mind' is a verb, as in minding the children.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind children is to care for and tend them.

clue.text: Unusually, he drew odd total out

indicators.note: unusually suggests something done in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man oddly drew a strange total.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast asleep or unconscious is the sense of out here.

clue.text: Get rid of letter — police are coming round

indicators.note: coming round means the whole string of letter, police and are is turned to read backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, plain-clothes police
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene where a letter must be destroyed before the police arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' turns the whole run backwards at once, not each piece, so the Greek letter ends the answer as ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something out entirely is to get rid of it completely.

clue.text: Record incidental music

definitions.meaning: to record points or a tally
the music written for a film or play

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves both as a verb for noting a tally and as the noun for a film's composed music.

clue.text: Subject of article by present writer

parts.note: the definite article
the person writing this clue refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: Asking what an article by the person now writing is about.
explanation.definitionFit: The topic of an essay or talk is its central subject.

clue.text: Grass — nearly always religiously kept cut to the minimum

indicators.note: each of the four words is cut down to the least it can be, a single opening letter

explanation.surface: Lawn grass that is almost always devoutly mown very short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like lawn but is the slang verb or noun for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a police informer is a grass, and the same word for a stool pigeon is synonymous.

clue.text: Crew forbidden to speak

indicators.note: to speak means the word for forbidden is said out loud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: something forbidden is banned

explanation.surface: A ship's crew under orders not to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people working or travelling together, such as a band of men, is a crew.

clue.text: Where to see stars in programme, with excellent value coming up

parts.note: a plan is a programme of action

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means excellent value is read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in letters
a rate is a price or value

explanation.surface: A TV programme featuring stars and excellent value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns AIRATE into ETARIA. Stars suggests celebrities but means heavenly bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Domed buildings projecting the night sky are where people view the heavens.

clue.text: Carried too far, old composer died

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian opera composer
d. is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: An elderly composer pushed himself too hard and died.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something to excess is to exaggerate it, carrying it too far.

clue.text: Free from prejudice. I lengthen shifts

indicators.note: shifts suggests the letters move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone extends their working shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate someone out of ignorance or bias is to free them from prejudice.

clue.text: Marathon leader's total disaster, as result of race mix-up

parts.note: Marathon is in Greece, and its leading letter M is the Greek letter mu

indicators.note: a disaster is a mess, so the letters of total are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A runner leading a marathon suffers total disaster after a mix-up in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' scrambles TOTAL into LATTO. The definition uses 'race' in its old ethnic sense; the term is now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The dated term describes a person of mixed black and white parentage, a mixture of ethnic groups.

clue.text: Nancy works as dairymaid brief spell of work

parts.note: a dairymaid milks the cows
op is short for operation, a stint of work

explanation.surface: Someone named Nancy is employed as a dairymaid for a short period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a girl's name; it is the dated slang for a weak, unmanly man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are old insults for a timid, effeminate man lacking courage.

clue.text: Poet's written a line with some force

parts.note: Ezra Pound was the American poet

explanation.surface: A poet writes a forceful line.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of force in the foot-pound-second system is so named.

clue.text: Queen on walkabout, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak tells us to read walkabout loosely as walk about, the about wrapping the word on

parts.note: read as walk + about: to march is to walk, and about puts it round the other word
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Queen meeting the crowds on one of her royal walkabouts.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter splits 'walkabout' as 'walk about', the 'about' wrapping 'on'; 'so to speak' admits the liberty of using half a word as an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen regnant is a reigning sovereign.

clue.text: Instruments produced by arbitrators after a month

indicators.note: after places the arbitrators behind the month in the answer

parts.note: Mar is the short form of March
ACAS is Britain's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service

explanation.surface: Musical instruments produced by mediators one month later.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the UK body that mediates industrial disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Latin American rattles, percussion instruments shaken in pairs.

clue.text: Give way to eastern pundit

parts.note: to sag is to sink or give way

explanation.surface: Deferring to a wise man from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A wise person or learned expert is a pundit.

clue.text: Sound contented, having turned up with bishop

indicators.note: turned means the word up is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

explanation.surface: Someone happy at having arrived to visit the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat makes this low vibrating noise when it is content.

clue.text: Disconcerted as result of being reported

indicators.note: being reported means the phrase is heard rather than written, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: through can mean because of, as a result of

explanation.surface: Someone upset because of what was said about them in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is to confuse or unsettle them, so the past tense means unsettled.

clue.text: One turns round and round, up and down

indicators.note: the clue says the word reads the same whether taken upwards or downwards in a down entry

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that spins and also reads both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blade assembly, spins.

clue.text: Mistaken belief held by army theoreticians

indicators.note: held by means the letters sit inside the words army theoreticians

explanation.surface: A false idea held by military thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A widely held but false notion is a fiction or fallacy.

clue.text: Record number of competitors

definitions.meaning: an item written in a log or ledger
the field of entrants in a race or contest

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a single item in a register and the total field signed up for a contest.

clue.text: Painter using a red Corot developed

indicators.note: developed suggests something worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; Corot was a French landscape painter

explanation.surface: An artist working with a red tone, as Corot developed his landscapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' and 'Corot' suggest fine art, but the answer is a house painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who paints and papers rooms in homes is a painter by trade.

clue.text: Little house within land borders rebuilt without restriction

indicators.note: within says the little house sits inside the rearranged letters
rebuilt suggests something reconstructed, so the letters of land borders are rearranged

parts.note: ho is the short form of house, as in addresses

explanation.surface: A small cottage on the boundary of an estate is reconstructed with no limits set.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrestling idiom for a bout with no banned grips means anything goes, free of any restriction.
